topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer opens the session by connecting the material to previous practicals and presenting the lecture's learning outcomes.

topics.label: Tumor viruses, oncogene capture, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of transforming tumor viruses and retroviral gene capture led to laboratory assays for identifying cellular oncogenes.

topics.label: Mechanisms and classifications of cancer-causing mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the major classes of cancer mutations and demonstrate how oncogenic, tumor-suppressive, and dominant-negative alterations disrupt cellular control pathways.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how defects in DNA repair pathways, replication machinery, and chromosome segregation generate sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer cells.

topics.label: Stepwise tumor progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the stepwise accumulation of mutations driving tumorigenesis and how inherited germline mutations accelerate cancer development.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by offering to take questions, suggesting recommended reading, and previewing the next lecture.
